subject: Gilmore Health post-demo: model behavior recap and guardrail plan
messages:
From: Avery Smith <avery@gilmorehealth.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Dr. Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@gilmorehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: demo + model fit questions

Hi Irene / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — useful run through. A couple quick notes and asks so our security/compliance folks can triage:

- Primary use case: triage assistant for outpatient intake (symptom intake + recommended care pathways). Will ingest partial PHI (patient age, symptoms, limited notes).
- Top concern from Lina: how the model handles sensitive prompts (self-harm mentions, suicidal ideation, substance misuse). We need concrete refusal/hand-off behaviors and examples.
- Operational ask: can you share the model candidates you recommend for this workload, plus any benchmark artifacts we can run locally? We want to reproduce latency and hallucination checks.
- Can you also provide the prompt sets you used in the demo and the safety probe set so we can run internal regressions?

Next steps from our side: Lina will coordinate security review; I will pull in procurement once we have cost estimates. Can we get the assets and a short runbook for testing by Wednesday EOD?

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Smith
Head of Product Integrations | Gilmore Health
Phone: +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: none in this message
From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Avery Smith <avery@gilmorehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Follow-up: demo + model fit questions

Hi Avery — great to meet you both. Short recap and the assets we promised.

Key recommendations (quick summary):
- Candidate models: redwood-chatlite-7b-q4f (best latency/cost balance), redwood-clarity-13b-q4 (stronger refusal/refusal-policy alignment), and open-aux-13b-rlhf (fallback for high-accuracy clinical reasoning).
- Safety profile: redwood-clarity-13b-q4 demonstrates better refusal consistency on our internal suicidal ideation probes (see safety_probe_matrix.xlsx). redwood-chatlite-7b-q4 is more likely to hallucinate medication advice in edge cases — we recommend conservative templated outputs + tool-based handoff for clinical recommendations.
- Suggested rollout: start with redwood-chatlite-7b-q4 behind a canary with the safety probe set, then widen to redwood-clarity for higher-sensitivity flows.

Attached: gilmore_eval_prompt_set.csv (sample prompts + expected tokens), safety_probe_matrix.xlsx (probe results summary), initial-benchmark-report.pdf (latency/throughput on 8k context). Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleBenchmarkFolder

Action items we took:
- Ben will own the refusal probe expansion and add a targeted set for self-harm phrasing variants.
- Marissa will put together an A/B plan for canary rollout and monitoring signals (refusal rate, OOMs, latency p95).

Timeline: we can ship the prompt set + probe matrix today; Ben/Marissa will deliver the expanded probe pack and canary plan by Wednesday EOD (your timezone). If that works, let’s tentatively book a readout on Friday 11/05.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Attachments: gilmore_eval_prompt_set.csv (CSV), safety_probe_matrix.xlsx (Excel), initial-benchmark-report.pdf (PDF)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo + model fit questions (internal)

Quick internal note — copying the plan from the call and assigning owners.

- Safety probes: expand the self-harm cluster to ~120 permutations (colloquialisms, negations, partial statements, third-party mentions). Add explicit PHI-laden prompts to stress redaction and routing. (Owner: Ben)
- Regression concerns: request Gilmore run our initial-benchmark-report.pdf against their representative prompt set; we’ll compare hallucination / hallucination-recall metrics. If their internal baseline spikes, escalate to a canary with automatic fallback to a rule-based responder. (Owner: Marissa)
- Monitoring hooks: we need 3 telemetry signals shipped early: refusal_rate, user_reported_flag, model_confidence_estimate (proxy). Suggest retention 90 days for the pilot.

Ben: I can put together the probe expansion today and upload to the shared Drive folder. Marissa: can you sketch the canary yml (routes + percentage ramp) so we can share with Gilmore?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Avery Smith <avery@gilmorehealth.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Dr. Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@gilmorehealth.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Follow-up: demo + model fit questions

Irene / team — this is great, thanks for the quick turnaround.

Lina reviewed the safety_probe_matrix.xlsx and flagged the refusal wording examples as helpful. A few clarifying notes:
- We want the canary to start at 2% traffic and include a forced human-handoff for any prompt that triggers the self-harm cluster.
- For latency, our SLA target for the triage assistant is p95 < 800ms for typical 400-token exchanges; please confirm redwood-chatlite-7b-q4 meets that under your 8k context benchmarks.
- Procurement will need a ballpark for monthly cost at 50k queries/month (we can supply typical average token counts).

Next steps:
1) We’ll run the supplied prompt set today and share results.
2) Schedule the readout: Friday 2026-11-05 at 10:00am PT works for our team.

See you Friday — please send the canary yml and the expanded probe pack before EOD Wednesday.

Thanks,
Avery
